textbookText: 110. Newton's law of cooling states that the rate of loss of heat of a body is: A) Directly proportional to the temperature difference between the body and its surroundings (for small differences) B) Inversely proportional to the temperature difference C) Independent of temperature difference D) Proportional to the square of the surrounding temperature

111. Which combination correctly matches the extraordinary property of water relevant to heat storage? A) High specific heat capacity → oceans/lakes moderate coastal climates B) Low specific heat capacity → water heats up instantly C) Zero latent heat of vaporization → water boils without energy input D) Negative specific heat capacity → water cools while absorbing heat
112. 5 kg of ice at 0°C is converted completely to water at 0°C. Given latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 kJ/kg, the heat absorbed is: A) 1680 kJ B) 336 kJ C) 1680 J D) 67.2 kJ

113. A calorimeter is typically made of copper because copper: A) Has low specific heat capacity and high thermal conductivity, quickly reaching thermal equilibrium B) Has very high specific heat capacity, storing heat efficiently C) Is a poor conductor of heat, minimizing heat exchange D) Is transparent, allowing visual temperature readings

114. If equal masses of ice at 0°C and water at 0°C are mixed with hot water, which absorbs MORE heat overall to reach the same final temperature? A) The ice, because it must first absorb latent heat to melt before warming further B) The water, because it has higher specific heat capacity than ice C) Both absorb exactly equal heat D) Neither absorbs any heat since both start at 0°C
115. Which of these is NOT a correct unit for quantity of heat? A) Kelvin (K) — this is a unit of temperature, not heat energy B) Joule (J) C) Calorie (cal) D) Kilocalorie (kcal)

116. In cooling correction (radiation correction) experiments, why is it needed? A) To account for heat lost to surroundings during the time taken for mixing/measurement B) To account for heat generated by friction in the stirrer C) To convert between Celsius and Kelvin D) To correct for errors in the mass balance only

117. Why does a thermos flask (vacuum flask) keep liquids hot for longer (application of quantity of heat concepts)? A) The vacuum layer minimizes heat loss by conduction and convection, and silvered walls reduce radiation loss B) It has a very high specific heat capacity that absorbs the liquid's heat C) It actively generates heat to compensate for losses D) It converts heat into latent heat, storing it indefinitely

118. The relationship 1 calorie ≈ 4.2 joules is known as: A) The mechanical equivalent of heat (Joule's constant, J) B) The specific heat capacity of water C) The latent heat of fusion of water D) Newton's law of cooling constant

119. When steam at 100°C condenses to water at 100°C, it: A) Releases latent heat of vaporization to the surroundings B) Absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the surroundings C) Undergoes no energy change at all D) Instantly freezes
120. A metal block of mass 0.5 kg absorbs 900 J of heat and its temperature rises by 2°C. Its specific heat capacity is: A) 900 J/kg·K B) 450 J/kg·K C) 1800 J/kg·K D) 225 J/kg·K
